intro.say: When some things go into water, they seem to disappear. This is called dissolving!

rounds.say: Put a spoon of sugar in water and stir. The sugar breaks into bits too tiny to see. It has dissolved!
rounds.caption: sugar dissolves

rounds.say: Put sand in water and stir. The sand is still there and sinks to the bottom. Sand does not dissolve.
rounds.caption: sand does not dissolve

rounds.ask: You stir salt into water. What happens?

options.label: it grows bigger
options.why: Salt does not grow in water.

options.label: it turns to stone
options.why: Salt does not turn into stone.

rounds.explain: Salt breaks into tiny bits and mixes into the water, so it dissolves.

rounds.ask: Which one does NOT dissolve in water?

options.label: sugar
options.why: Sugar dissolves when you stir it.

options.label: salt
options.why: Salt dissolves in water.

rounds.explain: Stones stay hard and sit at the bottom; they do not dissolve.

rounds.ask: Sugar dissolved in your drink. Is the sugar still there?

options.label: no, it is gone
options.why: Taste it: it is still sweet!

rounds.explain: The sugar is still there in tiny bits; that is why the drink tastes sweet.
Salt and sugar dissolve; sand, stones and coins stay the same.

intro.say: Some tricks make things dissolve faster. Let us find them!

rounds.say: Stirring helps! When you stir, the water moves around the sugar and carries tiny bits away faster.
rounds.caption: stir

rounds.say: Warm water helps too. Sugar dissolves faster in warm tea than in cold water.
rounds.caption: warm water = faster

options.label: waiting without stirring
options.why: It will dissolve, but very slowly.

options.label: adding ice
options.why: Cold water makes it slower.

rounds.explain: Stirring moves the water around so the sugar dissolves faster.

rounds.ask: Which water will dissolve sugar the fastest?

options.label: icy water
options.why: Cold water is the slowest.

options.label: cool water
options.why: Cool water is slower than warm.

rounds.explain: Warm water dissolves sugar faster than cold water.

rounds.ask: Here is a glass of very cold water. Will sugar dissolve fast or slow?

options.label: fast
options.why: Cold water makes dissolving slower.

rounds.explain: In cold water, sugar dissolves slowly.

rounds.ask: You put salt in water. How could you make it dissolve quicker?

options.label: put it in the freezer
options.why: Cold makes it slower.

options.label: add sand
options.why: Sand does not help.

rounds.explain: Salt, sugar and coffee powder dissolve; rice, sponges and metal do not.

intro.say: Let us solve dissolving puzzles, and even get the salt back out of the water!

rounds.say: Small pieces dissolve faster than big lumps. Sugar grains dissolve quicker than one big sugar lump.
rounds.caption: small bits = faster

rounds.say: Salty water left in the sun slowly dries up. The water goes into the air, but the salt is left behind!
rounds.caption: the salt comes back

rounds.ask: A big lump or tiny grains of sugar: which dissolves faster?

options.label: a big lump
options.why: A big lump takes longer for water to break up.

rounds.explain: Tiny grains have lots of surfaces for the water to work on, so they dissolve faster.

rounds.ask: Which plan dissolves sugar the FASTEST?

options.label: cold water, no stirring
options.why: That is the slowest plan.

options.label: cold water, stirring
options.why: Stirring helps, but warm water would help even more.

rounds.explain: Warm water and stirring together make sugar dissolve the fastest.

rounds.ask: Salt water dries up in the sun. What is left in the dish?

options.label: nothing
options.why: The water goes, but not the salt.

options.label: sand
options.why: There was no sand in the water.

rounds.explain: The water dries up into the air, but the salt stays behind.

rounds.ask: Sand and water are mixed. How can you get the sand out?

options.label: stir faster
options.why: Stirring just swirls the sand around.

options.label: add sugar
options.why: Sugar would not remove the sand.

rounds.explain: Sand did not dissolve, so a sieve or filter can catch the grains.

rounds.ask: You keep adding sugar to a cup of water. What happens in the end?

options.label: it all dissolves forever
options.why: Water can only hold so much sugar.

options.label: the water turns to sugar
options.why: The water is still water.

rounds.explain: Water can only dissolve so much; after that, extra sugar sits at the bottom.

rounds.ask: Put the sugar water steps in order.
rounds.explain: First water, then sugar, then stir until it dissolves.
